investigation.title: Swarm Gateway 502 Blocking All Remote Agent Checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime)
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents feature checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-08-21T15:05–15:06Z with an identical 502 bad_gateway error: the production API's POST /api/agents call could not reach the swarm gateway ELB at the /v1/agents endpoint. Because the failure occurs before any agent is provisioned, zero required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) were collected, and all contract assertions are unverifiable.
investigation.rootCause: The swarm gateway — an AWS ELB in us-east-2 fronting the /v1/agents provisioning endpoint — was unreachable from the production API at the time of the eval run. Every remote-agents check depends on a successful POST to this gateway as its first step (evidenced by the runner calling createAgent at infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1885), so a single gateway-level failure cascades to all three sibling checks with the same error message. This is an infrastructure-layer failure localized to the swarm gateway / ELB, not a code defect in the eval runner itself. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact is confirmed only at the eval layer.

possibleCauses: Swarm gateway ELB in us-east-2 was down, misconfigured, or had no healthy targets at the time of the eval run — the most strongly supported cause given the explicit 'swarm gateway unreachable' error and identical failure across all three sibling checks.
Transient network partition or DNS resolution failure between the production API and the ELB, causing connection errors that the API surfaces as a 502 bad_gateway.

The ELB target group behind /v1/agents had all instances marked unhealthy (e.g., after a deployment, scaling event, or health-check misconfiguration), causing the load balancer to return 502 with no healthy backend.
A misconfigured or expired internal routing rule or security group change blocking traffic from the production API to the ELB in us-east-2.

Eval infrastructure misconfiguration (e.g., wrong base URL for the swarm gateway injected into the probe environment) — less likely given the error message contains a real ELB hostname and the failure is consistent across all three checks.

investigations.title: model-matrix eval failure: aura-gpt-5-5 returns 502/424 provider_account_unavailable
investigations.summary: The model-matrix eval failed because the aura-gpt-5-5 model returned a 502 Bad Gateway wrapping a 424 Failed Dependency with error code provider_account_unavailable, causing 1 of 2 models to fail and violating the allPassed=true and failedModelCount=0 assertions. The aura-claude-sonnet-4-6 model passed cleanly, confirming the failure is isolated to the aura-gpt-5-5 provider path and not a broad infrastructure or eval harness issue.
investigations.rootCause: The upstream model provider backing aura-gpt-5-5 was temporarily unreachable at the time of the eval run (2026-08-21T15:05:13Z). AURA's runtime API returned a 502 with an embedded 424 Failed Dependency and error code provider_account_unavailable, with the message explicitly stating "AURA is temporarily unable to reach the model provider. This is an issue on our side, not with your account or credits." This is a provider-side or AURA-to-provider connectivity failure localized to the aura-gpt-5-5 model route, not an eval infrastructure defect, not a misconfiguration, and not a user-facing account or credential problem.

possibleCauses: Transient provider-side outage or degradation for the model provider backing aura-gpt-5-5 at the time of the eval run — highest evidence strength, directly stated in the 424 error body (failed-check.evidence).

investigations.rootCause: The swarm gateway — an AWS ELB in us-east-2 fronting the /v1/agents provisioning endpoint — was unreachable from the production API at the time of the eval run. Every remote-agents check depends on a successful POST to this gateway as its first step (evidenced by the runner calling createAgent at infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1885), so a single gateway-level failure cascades to all three sibling checks with the same error message. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact is confirmed only at the eval layer.

investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-runtime, remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state) failed at 2026-08-21T15:06 with an identical 502 bad_gateway error indicating the swarm gateway ELB at /v1/agents was unreachable during agent provisioning. investigations.rootCause: The swarm gateway (an AWS ELB in us-east-2 fronting /v1/agents) was unreachable at the time of the eval run. Every remote-agents check that calls POST /api/agents received a 502 bad_gateway response with the message "swarm gateway unreachable during agent provisioning: error sending request for url (http://[REDACTED].elb.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/v1/agents)". Because agent creation failed immediately, no agent was provisioned, and the eval runner could not collect any of the five required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message), causing the expected-output contract to be fully unmet. This is an eval-infrastructure signal of a backend dependency outage localized to the swarm gateway; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
